title: You cannot be tried twice for the same offence
summary: Once you have been tried and either convicted or acquitted, you generally cannot be tried again for the same offence.
body_plain: The Constitution protects you from being tried again for a criminal offence for which you have already been convicted or acquitted, except on the order of a superior court in the course of an appeal. It also protects you from being tried again for a criminal offence for which you have been pardoned. This stops the authorities from repeatedly prosecuting a person for the same matter.
rights: You cannot be tried again for an offence you were already convicted or acquitted of (s.36(9)).
You cannot be tried again for an offence for which you have been pardoned (s.36(10)).
Only a superior court on appeal can revisit the matter.
do_list: Keep records of any past trial, judgment, or pardon.
Tell your lawyer if you are charged again for the same matter.
Raise the earlier outcome as a defence.
dont_list: Do not assume you can be endlessly recharged for the same offence.
Do not lose your court documents from an earlier case.

citations.source_name: 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
